correctness.rationale: For both indexed cubic graphs each edge has exactly four adjacent edges; two colours thus impose three exact sums. Subtracting the rim equations forces d_{i+2}=-d_i and the rung equation forces s_{i-1}+s_i=2. The all-zero d case contradicts consecutive rung equations. Otherwise s_i=1 for all i, b_i=1-a_i, a_{i+2}=1-a_i and c_i+c_{i+1}=1. Precisely four-step and two-step periods respectively give ordinary closure if and only if 4|n and twisted closure if and only if n=2 mod4. Three independent starting bits yield exactly eight. Explicit proper three-edge-colourings prove all other cases at most three and one colour is impossible. Boundary n=3 prism, n=2 Möbius checked. Reproduced exhaustive/MILP/constructive independent finite checks; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The research supplies a complete sharp invariant for two natural infinite cubic families rather than generic upper bounds: the same local period-four forced pattern is compatible with opposite congruence classes under untwisted versus twisted seam closure. It also classifies and exactly counts all optimal two-colour assignments, identifying a structural local-to-global obstruction. A named parity shift and rigidity law motivates the exact computation and can inform analogous graph-cover constructions.
